areas.description: Constrained-random and coverage-driven testbenches for blocks nobody has verified before. We care about the boring part: reproducible seeds, coverage that means something, and a signoff document that survives a hostile reader.
areas.title: FUNCTIONAL VERIFICATION

areas.description: Transforms and estimators that have to run in real time on a mid-range part: interpolated DFT, CORDIC magnitude and phase, rate-of-change estimation, decimation chains. Fixed point, error budgets written down before the RTL.

areas.description: Why the design missed by 180 ps, and what to do about it. Constraint hygiene, clock-domain crossings, retiming, floorplanning on FPGA and on open PDKs. Every closure is written up as a before/after with the actual reports attached.
areas.title: TIMING & PHYSICAL CLOSURE

areas.description: Sky130 and open flows are the only route to real physical design for a lab with no licence budget. We push small blocks through GDS to learn where the flow lies to you, and publish the failures too.

areas.description: Two benches, shared boards, one JTAG server, regression running on whatever machine is free. Access is the resource we are actually pooling, so the scripts that manage it are treated as first-class work.
areas.title: BRINGUP & LAB INFRASTRUCTURE

areas.title: VERIFICATION PEDAGOGY

pages.intro:
A student-run lab for ASIC and FPGA hardware verification. We exist because the tools, the boards and the mentorship are hard to get to alone — so we pool them, run real RTL through real flows, and publish everything we learn.

No coursework. No spectators. You take a block, you verify it, you sign it off.

sections.heading: INK · FIVE FRAMES
sections.kicker: MARK ── FIVE STAGES OF STANDING UP

sections.body:
He stands at the end of the pipeline and nothing gets past him unsigned. Not a block, not a bitstream, not a waiver somebody talked themselves into late on a Friday. If it has not been verified, it does not ship, and the person who wrote it is the one who has to say so out loud.

Timing closure has a price, and it is always paid in something you liked. A stage you were proud of gets retimed. A clever optimisation comes out because it cannot be proven. A constraint file gets read for the fourth time at midnight, and the fourth reading is the one that finds it.

We keep the plate on the wall because that price is the actual work. Everything else is waiting for a run to finish.

projects.shortSummary: LIF neuron array with event-driven routing. Spikes, not tensors.
projects.summary: A digital array of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons with event-driven routing between them. Spikes instead of tensors, so there are no multipliers in the datapath and the whole power argument rests on how sparse the traffic really is.
projects.title: NEUROMORPHIC SPIKING NETWORK

projects.summary: Software-defined autonomous mission vehicle. FPGA-native deterministic edge compute, formal safety, 3-tier HIL digital twin.
projects.title: SENTINEL

projects.shortSummary: The whole stack in fabric, no soft core in the data path.
projects.summary: The stack in fabric: MAC interface, ARP, IPv4 and a TCP state machine with retransmission, all in hardware with no soft core in the data path. It either holds line rate on a gigabit PHY or it does not count.
projects.title: TCP/IP IN FPGA

projects.summary: A weight-stationary grid of int8 MAC cells with tiled GEMM scheduling and a double-buffered activation store. The interesting engineering is the memory schedule; the multipliers are the easy part.
projects.title: SYSTOLIC ARRAY NEURAL NETWORK

projects.shortSummary: Lattice arithmetic and NTT butterflies, constant-time by construction.
projects.summary: Hardware for the algorithms that outlive RSA: lattice arithmetic, NTT butterflies, constant-time control and a sampler that does not leak through timing. The threat model is a machine that does not exist yet, which makes the constant-time argument the whole project.
projects.title: POST-QUANTUM CRYPTO IN FPGA

projects.summary: Instrumentation for the grid: a six-channel interpolated-DFT front end with CORDIC magnitude and phase and ROCOF differentiation, wrapped in the reporting protocols a substation actually expects. No vendor IP anywhere in the chain.
projects.title: POWER SYSTEM PROTOCOLS

projects.summary: Attitude control in fabric instead of firmware: IMU fusion, a fixed-point rate loop and PWM generation with deterministic latency from sample to actuator. The argument for hardware here is jitter, not throughput.
projects.title: DRONE CONTROL

projects.summary: Tick-to-trade in hardware: market-data feed parsing on the wire, an order book maintained in fabric and a decision path measured in nanoseconds. Every stage has to justify the cycle it costs.
